# Work, cost and material by period

The Portfolio archive can include native assignment values for explicit reporting periods. The existing PortfolioWorkspace reopens each selected immutable edition through its original MPXJ recipe. MPXJ calculates the values using that edition's native calendars, assignment rules and resource rates. The archive retains the complete calculation alongside its original project files and reporting tables.

Use this workflow for a completed-project reporting handover, a period-by-period cost/work review or a customer reporting dataset. Keep the selected editions, dates and financial interpretation in the published review. The ordinary project, task, resource and assignment tables remain available with their complete native fields.

## Select the source and periods

Open the original migration desk and choose **Portfolio archive**. Create or open the intended cohort. Select one actual immutable edition for each project, with a stable project key. Read the original field definitions after changing that selection.

Enable **Include native period reporting**. The panel accepts either generated daily, weekly or monthly date periods or individually entered local date/time periods. The date generator fills the explicit period list; it does not change a project calendar or calculate a value. Review that list before saving. A monthly series keeps the original day-of-month anchor and uses the month's last date when that day is absent.

Every period has a unique key, readable label and exact native start/finish bounds. Ranges use the project's original local date/time and must be ordered, nonempty and nonoverlapping in duration. The native boundary rule depends on the operation: duration overlap excludes the finish; instantaneous cost accrual can include both endpoints and selects the first matching range. At adjoining boundaries that can place a cost in the earlier period. These original native results are retained without redistribution. No timezone conversion or assumption that a working day is eight hours is made.

For an actual pro-rata COST resource with nonzero actual cost, MPXJ's selected original method derives a fixed whole-minute stride from the first range. This workflow therefore requires equal-width contiguous ranges with a positive whole-minute stride for the affected COST, ACTUAL_COST and ACTUAL_REGULAR_COST series. Unequal calendar months, gaps and sub-minute intervals are rejected before entering that native method. Select a fixed daily/weekly grid or change the reviewed series selection. The admission also bounds that method's internal alignment/full-assignment walk to 100,000 steps per assignment and two million estimated steps for the selected calculation. Its exact admitted basis is retained. Other supported native paths keep their original range semantics.

For example:

    {
      "key": "2026-10",
      "label": "October 2026",
      "start": "2026-10-01T00:00:00",
      "finish": "2026-11-01T00:00:00"
    }

The native calculation uses these exact boundaries. The original source must contain the intended project schedule and resource/calendar basis for that period. A valid empty period can produce native null values; the application retains that result.

A profile accepts 1–3,660 periods and 1–32 named series. The complete selected cohort is limited to 2,000,000 assignment × period × series facts. A larger reporting request should use a deliberately narrower period/series selection or separate reporting cohorts, each with its own source and review.

## Choose native series

Each series has a unique report name, an actual AssignmentField name, a kind and, for work, an explicit native unit. The selector uses the original field catalogue from the chosen editions. It rejects a kind that conflicts with any selected edition's native definition.

| Kind | Native definition | Calculation and grouping |
| --- | --- | --- |
| work | WORK | Original ResourceAssignment.getTimephasedDurationValues, with selected TimeUnit; unit and elapsed status remain separate. |
| money | CURRENCY | Original ResourceAssignment.getTimephasedNumericValues; native or explicitly reviewed project currency remains part of the group. |
| material | NUMERIC or UNITS | Original numeric period method for an actual material resource; each resource identity and material label remains separate. |

Supported selections include current, actual, remaining, planned and budget work/cost fields where present, regular/overtime variants, and baseline 0–10 work/cost/material and baseline-budget work/cost fields. Material selections include the native MATERIAL, ACTUAL_MATERIAL, REMAINING_MATERIAL and PLANNED_MATERIAL families where present. A name appearing in the source catalogue is still checked against the supported period-method field set.

Work units are MINUTES, HOURS, DAYS, WEEKS, MONTHS and YEARS, plus their ELAPSED_ forms. MPXJ performs the actual requested conversion against the native project settings. Material and money do not take a work-unit setting.

This minimal profile selects exact work and cost series:

    {
      "schema": "portfolio.timephased-profile.v1",
      "periods": [
        {
          "key": "2026-10",
          "label": "October 2026",
          "start": "2026-10-01T00:00:00",
          "finish": "2026-11-01T00:00:00"
        }
      ],
      "series": [
        {"name": "current_work", "field": "WORK", "kind": "work", "units": "HOURS"},
        {"name": "current_cost", "field": "COST", "kind": "money"},
        {"name": "baseline_cost", "field": "BASELINE_COST", "kind": "money"}
      ]
    }

Save it as the cohort profile's **timephased** property. Existing columns, scalar metrics and currency declarations keep their original meaning. See examples/timephased-profile.json and examples/timephased-cohort.json for complete editable inputs.

## Review and publish

Save the cohort through its existing saved-action workflow. Review the exact saved revision. A first native period review requires the selected original MPXJ 16.10.0 runtime and the complete source objects already retained by the PortfolioWorkspace.

The native-project context holds the original runtime lock and reconstructs the original source recipe. It checks the actual assignment/task/resource identities against the retained model. Before a calculation, the original raw timephased source, resource detail/rate basis, field definitions and runtime identity must match that edition. The complete assignment effective calendar is retained even when MPXJ derives a calendar that has no standalone source calendar row. Baseline series use the actual ProjectFile.getBaselineCalendar value, including its native named-calendar/default fallback; that complete definition and source resolution are separately retained. Each series and fact identifies its calendar basis.

Each selected source gets an immutable, bounded JSONL calculation object. Its header binds the edition, model, source objects, recipe, complete period profile and runtime. Ordered assignment/series records retain every native value or null. The final footer records completion and counts. The original operator store publishes the complete object by its content address.

A completed calculation is reused by the original action. If an action loses its reply, reopen its saved request and continue that request. A complete stored calculation never requires a replacement native calculation. An interrupted calculation that has no accepted complete object can be regenerated from the same original edition and profile. No remote target write or project scheduling change is involved.

The review shows the complete assignment/fact counts, capture identities, native errors, table hashes and a bounded preview of period totals. **Open complete period totals**, **Open original assignment values** and **Open calendars and rate basis** page through the original publication tables. The full CSVs and database include every row.

Publish the exact review with the reviewer and a concrete delivery decision. An edited selection, period, series or currency declaration requires a following review. Existing lost-reply, same-request and revision guards remain in effect.

## Interpret the values

The native period facts use **assignment grain**. They link to the actual source task and resource. Task-only fixed costs remain in their task fields and are outside these assignment totals. A scalar task/project measure can be reported separately, with its own grain; do not add it to the assignment total as another contribution to the same sum.

Each fact records one state:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| native_value | The original method returned a supported numeric or duration value, retained as exact text with its typed native value. |
| native_null | The original method returned null for that assignment, series and period. |
| not_applicable | The selected dimension does not apply to this actual resource type, such as work for a material resource. |
| native_error | The original method raised an error, retained with its original message and series identity. |
| unsupported_native_value | A returned value cannot be interpreted as the selected supported dimension; its full original representation remains retained. |

Native null is distinct from zero. An all-null total has no invented zero total. Totals include value, null, inapplicable and error counts so the reader can assess completeness. Native errors and unsupported values are visible in the review and retained facts.

Totals use exact decimal addition of original numeric text. Work groups preserve selected units and elapsed true/false. Money groups preserve project currency and its original or explicitly declared source. Unknown currencies remain project-local groups. Material groups retain the actual resource identity as well as its label; two resources with the same displayed unit are not automatically combined.

The raw source spans can use a duration representation for material quantities. Their explicit dimension, resource type, full typed values and separate native material-period calculation preserve that distinction. Raw amount-per-hour and span totals are source evidence, not a second set of period contributions to add to the calculated values.

## Reporting tables and joins

The original relational tables remain complete. A timephased profile adds these tables:

| Table | Complete retained content |
| --- | --- |
| timephased_source_sets | Every original RAW_TIMEPHASED field, definition, state, source pointer and span count. |
| timephased_spans | Every raw span, local bounds, amount per hour, total amount, units, elapsed status and full typed value. |
| resource_rate_entries | Every resource cost-rate table entry and its dated range/cost-per-use. |
| resource_rate_values | Each rate within an entry, with original amount, TimeUnit and source currency. |
| resource_availability | Complete original resource availability intervals and units. |
| calendar_rules | Working week, exceptions, work weeks and native unit-conversion definitions. |
| timephased_captures | Complete calculation-object identity, byte hash, runtime, profile, source binding, baseline calendar and native input admission. |
| timephased_periods | Exact ordered reporting ranges and original overlap/accrual boundary semantics. |
| timephased_series | Named series, native fields/definitions, calculation methods, calendar basis, boundary semantics and assignment grain. |
| timephased_assignment_basis | Actual task/resource links, effective native calendar, selected cost-rate table and resource-rate source identity. |
| timephased_values | Every assignment × series × period value, null or error. |
| timephased_totals | Exact grouped totals and complete state counts. |

Facts join their assignment, basis, period and series by retained IDs. Assignment basis links to actual task/resource entity IDs, with explicit resolution status. Assignment effective and project baseline calendars retain complete native JSON and a source calendar entity when uniquely resolved. Each native series/fact names the applicable basis. Derived native calendars remain usable as complete definitions without a guessed source join.

All tables use the original edition-local identities. Their columns remain TEXT in CSV, SQLite and the generated Azure SQL schema so large IDs, precision, ISO local dates, native units and JSON survive the handover. The generated data dictionary includes the additional tables and exact headers. Power Query uses those same complete headers.

## Query and export

Use the original Archive table/query interface and saved query-export action. A useful period report is:

    SELECT project_key, period_key, series, currency, units, elapsed,
           material_resource_entity_id, total_text,
           value_rows, null_rows, not_applicable_rows, error_rows
    FROM timephased_totals
    ORDER BY project_key, period_key, series, currency, units,
             material_resource_entity_id;

For a selected series, filter by its retained report name with a parameter. The original query preview is bounded; **Export complete query** streams every matching row. examples/timephased-query.sql and examples/timephased-parameters.json provide that input.

For a further sum, use the original decimal_sum function only after choosing the complete grouping dimensions. Keep project, series/field definition, currency/currency source, units/elapsed and material resource identity where applicable. Values from cumulative/alternative fields or overlapping business reporting selections need an explicit consuming-model decision.

The HTML report shows selected series/periods, native capture identities and a labeled totals preview with links to every full table. The complete ZIP includes CSV, SQLite, Power Query, Azure SQL definitions, source evidence and the operating guide. Load the supplied Power Query against the unpacked archive folder, then build the customer's reporting model from its reviewed dimensions.

## Portable receiving

Receive the complete ZIP through the existing Archive upload, inspect and receive actions. The archive carries the original project/companion/model closure plus every selected complete calculation object under source/operator-objects. Source hashes, calculation bindings, record order, headers, footer and file stability are verified while streaming.

Before accepting the received cohort, the original receiver rebuilds every reporting row and exact total from the restored editions and retained calculation records. It compares those results with the publication's full table hashes and review. It requires no JVM or target credentials for this operation. The received original source remains available if a later operator deliberately creates a new native calculation.

The complete original archive and uncompressed closure retain the existing 8 GiB receiving limit. Individual calculation objects are bounded at 2 GiB and JSONL records at 64 MiB; streams and temporary SQLite aggregation keep large facts out of a whole-file memory allocation.

Keep the same receiving request, original archive identity and destination after an interruption. A completed request reopens its receipt even after the intake filename has moved. Subsequent source-local browsing, full query export and workspace handover use the retained original data.

## Native receiving continuation

Continue from the same MPXJ runtime and workspace used for source intake. For the supplied timephased-budget-baseline.mpp fixture, select the actual edition ID returned by that intake.

Follow native/README.md. The optional --native-timephased argument derives an explicit weekly profile from that actual fixture's retained raw span bounds and supported native definitions. --timephased-profile selects an already-reviewed explicit profile instead. Both extend the same original archive receiving function and browser helper.

The native phase enters the profile through the real Archive controls, retains the original save/review/publish actions, exports complete totals, downloads the full handover, receives it into the original fresh workspace and reopens it with native calculation access disabled. It checks the original source models and calculation/table identities. Its actual result, screenshots and saved requests belong in the original operation and customer handover.

## Primary native contract

The selected runtime is MPXJ 16.10.0 at upstream commit 7ef9e72813d33378c55ec6ceb148cc831ed22033. Original methods, field definitions and fixture identities are listed in SOURCE_REFERENCES.json.

- [MPXJ timephased data guide](https://www.mpxj.org/howto-use-timephased/)
- [ResourceAssignment API](https://javadoc.io/doc/net.sf.mpxj/mpxj/16.10.0/org/mpxj/ResourceAssignment.html)
- [AssignmentField source at the selected commit](https://github.com/joniles/mpxj/blob/7ef9e72813d33378c55ec6ceb148cc831ed22033/src/main/java/org/mpxj/AssignmentField.java)
- [TimephasedItem API](https://javadoc.io/doc/net.sf.mpxj/mpxj/16.10.0/org/mpxj/TimephasedItem.html)

# Portfolio archive and reporting

This component extends the original PortfolioWorkspace and migration desk with a complete reporting cohort: selected project editions, a native field review, exact-grain measures, relational CSV and SQLite tables, a portable source archive, Power Query and SQL setup, and source-preserving receiving.

The same desk retains the original project files, companion captures, edits, target calls and source reviews. Open **Portfolio archive** in that running desk. The command-line operations below use its existing action IDs and recovery history.

## Select the original projects

Intake project files through the original Source section or existing intake action. MPXJ remains the native reader. For already-retired Project Online systems, use the customer's retained files and enterprise exports. An archive operation reads saved editions; it does not extract a retired service.

Choose one immutable edition per business project. Give it a stable project key and a readable label. A cohort can contain 1–500 distinct editions; the same edition cannot be counted twice as different projects. Use a separate cohort for another reporting date or alternative selection. The original source remains available alongside every following edition.

For each companion file, select its label, role, format, encoding, delimiter and JSON pointer before intake. The stored profile records those decisions. The Source page shows actual captured rows and column keys. A companion mapping names its exact capture, source identity column, native family and original target field. Key, UID and GUID matching remains confined to that original project edition. All mapped before and after values go through the original source review. Distinct captures of the same bytes use their full capture selector.

## Review fields and measures

Read the actual native field definitions for the selected editions. Standard available fields are used when columns are omitted. Explicit column selection supports up to96 fields per family; the full fields and field_definitions tables retain every captured field and definition regardless of that selection.

Choose one aggregation grain:

- **Project properties:** use the original singular project row.
- **Leaf tasks:** use native task rows after excluding summary rows and rows that are parents of another original task.
- **Assignments:** use original assignment rows, with their native task and resource links.

Each measure names an actual native field and its intended kind. Currency fields require the money kind; WORK, DURATION and DELAY require work; NUMERIC, INTEGER and SHORT allow number. Rates, percentages and resource units retain their complete original values in the fields table and do not become money or additive work through a numeric encoding. Conflicting native definitions across selected editions appear in the review.

Totals use Decimal on the original numeric text, with precision expanded for the complete sum. Native currency codes keep separate groups. When a source lacks a code, an operator can declare a three-letter currency with a concrete source note; otherwise that project's amounts remain in their own unspecified-currency group. Native duration units are preserved without an assumed hours-per-day conversion. Elapsed true, false and unspecified remain distinct. Missing, unsupported and excluded rows are reported with the complete per-row contribution records.

Save the cohort, review its complete projection, then publish that exact review with an operator name and delivery decision. An edited cohort requires a following review. The publication retains the original review digest, selected editions, source model identities, table row hashes and reporting approval.

## Native period reporting

The same cohort can include original MPXJ assignment work, cost and material values for explicit local reporting periods. Enable **Include native period reporting**, read the selected field definitions and choose periods/series before saving. The original native runtime calculates the exact selected edition; complete raw spans, effective calendars, dated resource rates, values/nulls and grouped totals travel with the archive. Portable receiving verifies that saved calculation and every projected row without a JVM.

[TIMEPHASED.md](TIMEPHASED.md) explains the full native period selection, assignment grain, units/currency/material grouping, table joins, exact SQL and original receiving continuation. Existing scalar metrics retain their selected grain and complete contribution tables.

## The delivered archive

The complete ZIP includes:

- Original selected editions, their source and parent editions, original reviews and native readback comparisons.
- Every referenced native project file and companion file, the exact captured models and complete JsonWriter output.
- Original MsPlanner capture pages, expanded collection continuations, combined native reader responses and probe objects when a selected edition came through the native target reader.
- CSV tables, a SQLite reporting database, an HTML report and a complete data dictionary.
- Power Query M, an Azure SQL table script and operating instructions.
- A manifest naming the exact byte count, SHA-256 and role of every member, with the original cohort review and approval.

The complete selected closure is included. Each source object remains named by its existing SHA identity. Original request records, broader company case records and unrelated projects are not pulled into the reporting cohort.

The table families are projects, tasks, resources, assignments, dependencies, calendars, fields, field_definitions, relationships, native_collections, sources, findings, companion_sources, companion_columns, companion_rows, companion_cells, companion_links, measure_totals and measure_contributions.

Entity IDs combine the original edition, family and source key. Relationships resolve native IDs within that edition only. Ambiguous or missing identities remain explicit rows and findings. Calendar relations use captured ProjectCalendar references or actual CALENDAR_UNIQUE_ID fields; calendar definitions and native detail collections remain complete. Companion records retain original line/record positions, column keys, exact JSON numeric text, and their mapping to original native entities.

## Inspect and query a publication

The Archive tab pages through a selected completed publication, supports text filtering and opens each complete row. Downloads contain all rows. The query preview returns up to250 rows; the full query export streams every result into an immutable CSV.

All relational columns use SQLite TEXT and CSV text. This preserves precision, original ISO dates, local times, native units, leading zeros, identifiers and complete JSON. The SQL interface allows read-only SELECT/WITH expressions over the declared tables. It disables writes and extension loading. Use decimal_sum for exact decimal totals, with explicit grouping by currency, unit and elapsed status:

    SELECT currency, units, elapsed, decimal_sum(total_text) AS exact_total
    FROM measure_totals
    WHERE metric = ?
    GROUP BY currency, units, elapsed
    ORDER BY currency, units, elapsed

Bind a text parameter such as ["current_cost"]. Do not combine rows from alternative grains or cumulative source fields without an explicit business decision. The contribution table provides the exact selected rows.

Power Query reads the original UTF-8 CSV using QuoteStyle.Csv, requires its complete expected header list and keeps columns as text. Select the unpacked archive folder, then choose the desired table from the generated query result. Apply business-specific currency/date conversions in the consuming model after reviewing their source definitions. The Azure SQL script defines the same text columns; run it in a selected existing database and load the original CSVs through the customer's approved import process.

## Existing CLI

Use the product root and its operator directory on PYTHONPATH, as for the original migration desk:

    PYTHONPATH=/path/to/project-portfolio-migration:/path/to/project-portfolio-migration/operator \
      python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace state

List source fields or saved cohorts:

    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace \
      archive-fields <edition-sha256> [<another-edition-sha256>]
    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace cohort
    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace cohort <cohort-id>

The existing action command owns every mutation:

    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace \
      action archive_save --request-id <retained-64hex-id> --arguments-file cohort.json

A cohort definition contains name, description, members and profile. Example members:

    {
      "name": "Completed customer projects",
      "description": "Preserve the selected closing editions for reporting",
      "members": [
        {
          "project_key": "customer-project-a",
          "label": "Customer Project A",
          "edition_id": "<actual-original-edition-sha256>",
          "currency": {"code": "GBP", "note": "Code confirmed from the retained project accounting export"}
        }
      ],
      "profile": {
        "metrics": {
          "grain": "leaf_tasks",
          "measures": [
            {"name": "current_cost", "field": "COST", "kind": "money"},
            {"name": "planned_work", "field": "WORK", "kind": "work"}
          ]
        }
      }
    }

Use actual fields shown by archive-fields. Omit currency when the native source supplies the code. Editing a cohort also passes cohort_id and its exact expected_revision.

Next action arguments are:

| Original action | Exact selected arguments |
| --- | --- |
| archive_review | cohort_id, expected_revision |
| archive_publish | cohort_id, expected_revision, review_sha256, reviewer, note |
| archive_query_export | cohort_id, publication_id, sql, parameters |
| archive_inspect | source returned by the original upload |
| archive_receive | source, manifest_sha256 from inspection, reviewer, note |

Read the same saved action with request <request-id>; resume it with request <request-id> --resume. A lost reply never needs a new action ID. The operation stores complete arguments and original results, and the cohort index includes the same request's immutable mutation receipt.

Read a table or query from a selected publication:

    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace \
      archive-table <cohort-id> <publication-id> measure_totals --limit 50
    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace \
      archive-query <cohort-id> <publication-id> --sql-file query.sql --parameters-file parameters.json

Copy any artifact using its actual returned SHA:

    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/customer-workspace \
      artifact <sha256> --output /delivery/portfolio-archive.zip

## Receive and reopen

Upload a complete reporting ZIP through the Archive page or the original CLI's archive input:

    python3 -m portfolio_target.cli --workspace /private/received-workspace \
      upload /delivery/portfolio-archive.zip --archive

Use that exact upload result in archive_inspect, read the complete inspection, then pass its manifest_sha256 to archive_receive with the receiving operator and note. This admits archives up to8GiB and validates at most8GiB of complete uncompressed members. Individual project-file intake retains its original limit. Large CLI transfers and original object hashing use bounded chunks.

Receiving validates every member before original object adoption, rejects path/member aliases, restores the exact native records and objects, verifies SQLite integrity/schema/row hashes, then recalculates the reporting projection from the restored native editions. The same archive's byte identities and the same request remain stable through interruption. Source objects use their original store IDs; cohort publication, incoming review and receiving decision remain distinct retained records.

The new cohort opens in the same Archive tab. Original models and source files can be inspected without the initial upload paths or remote target credentials. Already completed receiving returns the original receipt before touching removed intake files. The broader original portable-workspace export remains available for a full operator workspace handover.

## Native receiving continuation

native/receive.py and native/browser.mjs extend the original equipped portfolio receiving operation with the reporting workflow. They consume actual editions from that operation, preserve deterministic original action IDs and checkpoints, exercise the full CSV/SQLite/query/package/source-absent receive path, and use the same authenticated browser and original action API. Keep the parent operation's selected MPXJ runtime, source fixtures and provider custody.

# Original native archive receiving

This is a following phase of the existing equipped portfolio receiving operation. It uses the actual project editions retained by that operation, the same complete PortfolioWorkspace and the existing migration desk. Its input is saved native MPXJ output; it does not acquire another project or submit a target operation.

## Select the completed source

Keep the parent operation's original workspace, operation ID, current complete product source and native result files. Read the actual edition IDs returned by that operation. Select distinct original projects for a portfolio cohort. An alternative corrected edition of a project belongs in a separate comparison cohort.

The receiving function derives labels and available COST, ACTUAL_COST and WORK measures from the actual captured project model and field definitions. Unsupported fields are omitted from that example profile. Complete native fields and definitions still enter the relational delivery.

Use the original MPXJ runtime if it is already injected into the parent process. This archive phase reads retained models and needs no additional native file conversion. Its original authenticated desk obtains a fresh local token at each reopen.

## Join the same original operation

From the complete product root:

    python3 archive/native/receive.py \
      --workspace /private/original-portfolio-workspace \
      --edition <actual-first-native-edition-sha256> \
      --edition <actual-second-native-edition-sha256> \
      --output /private/original-native-output/archive \
      --operation-id <same-original-native-receiving-operation> \
      --node /path/to/node \
      --playwright /path/to/playwright/index.mjs \
      --chromium /path/to/chrome-headless-shell

One original edition is sufficient for a single-project handover. The output directory must be outside the original workspace. The receiver creates its own received-workspace inside that output and retains all source and receiving artifacts there.

An already running Python receiver can call the same phase directly:

    from archive.native.receive import receive_archive

    result = receive_archive(
        original_workspace,
        actual_edition_ids,
        original_output / "archive",
        operation_id=original_operation_id,
        node=node_path,
        playwright=playwright_module_path,
        chromium=chromium_path,
        native=original_portfolio.native,
    )

The module imports operator/native/receive.py and reuses its running_desk, browser_receive, artifact verification and browser lifetime. The original operator/native/browser.mjs hands the archive phases to archive/native/browser.mjs after establishing the same workspace identity and saved action state. It does not start a second server or browser inside that handoff.

On Linux, the original browser's temporary files stay in one process-private /dev directory. The source, workspace, operation record, downloads, screenshots and final receipts must be in a durable selected directory. Keep one receiver attached to this original phase.

## The complete journey

The first phase creates a cohort through the actual Archive UI, selects the actual retained editions, saves the selected profile and deliberately loses the completed save reply. The existing action history rejoins that same request. It then reviews and publishes the complete cohort, reads native task rows, runs a read-only SQL query, exports every result and downloads the complete archive, SQLite database, HTML report, data dictionary, Power Query, Azure SQL script and operating guide.

The following fresh workspace uploads that exact archive, inspects all original members and receives it through the actual UI. This phase loses one completed receive reply and rejoins its original request. Publication, archive, review and source edition identities are compared with the first workspace.

The receiver then moves only its owned intake filename to a retained sibling. All original source objects remain in the received stores. The same completed receiving request must return its original result without the intake filename. Every selected complete native model is compared with the original workspace. The desk finally reopens again, reads its saved cohort, inspects the native rows and reruns the reporting query without source uploads.

Desktop and mobile captures use widths 1440 and 390. Screenshots and downloaded files are retained atomically and verified against their saved hashes. If a carrier ends before the deliberate lost-reply marker can be saved, the original helper records the actual carrier-recovery outcome while continuing the same action.

## Resume and consume

Rerun the exact command with the same workspace, selected editions, output and operation ID. Completed phase results verify and reuse the original artifacts. Pending action IDs remain in the original browser and workspace histories. When an original action is retained as FAILED and its concrete cause has been repaired, --resume-failed asks the existing action API to continue that same request.

The final result is output/result.json. Its schema is portfolio.archive-native-receiving-result.v1 and state is COMPLETE. It contains:

- The original operation, selected native editions, labels and exact metric profile.
- Original, received and reopened phase results.
- Exact cohort, publication, review and archive identities.
- The original save, review, publish, query-export, inspect and receive request IDs.
- The source-absent same-request replay.
- Complete file paths, byte counts and SHA-256 values for every returned artifact.

operation.json pins the selected source and original operation. selected-profile.json records the actual native metric choices. source-selection.json and its retained history identify the source used at each continuation. The original, received and reopened subdirectories retain their browser action checkpoints, storage state, downloaded delivery files and screenshots.

Use these outputs for the existing customer's handover and the same parent operation's result. The commercial case and target execution history remain in their original workflows.

## Following native timephased reporting phase

Use the actual edition returned for the original upstream
junit/data/timephased-budget-baseline.mpp fixture. The parent operation already
owns its native intake and runtime. Preserve its exact edition/workspace and
original receiving operation ID.

Add --native-timephased to this same archive receiving command and choose an
owned following output directory such as original-native-output/archive-timephased.
The flag selects explicit weekly intervals from the actual retained raw span
bounds, rounded outward to complete equal-width weeks, and supported native WORK/CURRENCY/material field definitions. A saved
explicit selection may instead be supplied with --timephased-profile profile.json.
The two flags are mutually exclusive.

    python3 archive/native/receive.py \
      --workspace /private/original-portfolio-workspace \
      --edition <actual-timephased-fixture-edition-sha256> \
      --output /private/original-native-output/archive-timephased \
      --operation-id <same-original-native-receiving-operation> \
      --native-timephased \
      --node /path/to/node \
      --playwright /path/to/playwright/index.mjs \
      --chromium /path/to/chrome-headless-shell

An already equipped original Python receiver calls receive_archive with its same
arguments plus timephased=True, or timephased=<complete selected profile dict>.
Pass native=original_portfolio.native so the original runtime is reused.

This phase enters periods and named series through the actual Archive controls.
Its first native review retains full original calculation records and requires
no native calculation errors for the selected fixture. The browser verifies
complete assignment facts/period totals, runs and exports the full totals query,
downloads the complete source/reporting ZIP and retains desktop/phone views.

The following receive/reopen phases inject RetainedCalculationOnly, whose native
lookup, lock and ensure methods fail if invoked. Successful receiving therefore
demonstrates source/calculation/table verification without a second native
calculation. The original selected models, complete JSONL objects, archive and
query rows remain unchanged. Source-absent same-request receiving is preserved.

Keep the same operation/output/edition/profile arguments for a continuation.
selected-profile.json pins the actual generated periods and fields. Existing
completed source and browser phase receipts are verified and reused. The
result's profile.timephased and original publication identify this following
reporting delivery; native receipt and customer screens must come from the
same accepted original operation.

The receiving result retains both assignment effective calendars and the actual

# Receive the complete portfolio target desk

This receiving workflow opens the actual operator server and the original MPXJ 16.10.0 source engine. It uses one selected original project file, retains its source edition, corrects an actual task's native NAME field, prepares and reviews the file target, writes Project XML with the original MSPDIWriter, receives those exact bytes through the original reader, records every observed difference, and completes the handover and portable restore.

The browser runs at desktop and mobile widths. It discards one real local intake HTTP reply after the server returns it, then recovers that same saved request. The accepted source edition, target plan, native export, capture, comparison, acceptance, report and original action IDs stay in the same workspace.

## Select the original runtime and input

Use the original portfolio runtime and its actual MPXJ distribution. The application calls NativeMPXJ.ensure(); Java, JPype and MPXJ must already be available to that runtime. Use the existing Node, Playwright and Chromium installation and the same admitted native receiving operation.

Pinned small upstream input options at joniles/mpxj commit 7ef9e72813d33378c55ec6ceb148cc831ed22033 are:

| Original fixture | Git blob |
| --- | --- |
| junit/data/generated/assignment-assignments/assignment-assignments-project2019-mspdi.xml | 229c381968ee1b23d2027a20eff0983dab3e855b |

The exact selected file bytes and source SHA-256 are saved before intake. The browser chooses its task from the actual returned model and preserves the exact row key and typed before value. It does not select a guessed numeric UID.

## Continue the same operation

From the service directory, with actual absolute paths:

~~~bash
python3 operator/native/receive.py \
  --workspace /absolute/portfolio-receiving/workspace \
  --source /absolute/mpxj/assignment-assignments-project2019-mspdi.xml \
  --output /absolute/portfolio-receiving/output \
  --operation-id portfolio-target-receiving-001 \
  --node /absolute/existing/node \
  --playwright /absolute/existing/playwright/index.mjs \
  --chromium /absolute/existing/chrome-headless-shell
~~~

Keep the same operation ID, workspace and output directory when continuing an existing run.

The Python callable receive(..., native=existing_native) can join an already running original NativeMPXJ instance. It reuses that instance for both original and restored workspaces. The browser temporary directory stays within the same process's private /dev. Source, request progress, outputs and restore records remain at the selected durable output path.

If an original local action failed and its source has been corrected, the same command with --resume-failed invokes that action's existing resume path. Its original ID, input digest, failure history and retained native calls remain. A completed stage reopens its saved result and verifies its existing artifact bytes.

A source finding with requires_decision:true uses the original source review's exact finding SHA and decision shape. Supply a reviewed JSON file with --review-decisions when the selected source requires it. The actual source-review-findings.json is retained when source review requires further handling.

## What the operation retains

- operation.json binds the operation ID, selected workspace, source hash, reviewer and original decision input.
- native-runtime.json and source-selection.json identify the actual native runtime and the source used by the receiver.
- original/browser-progress.json records each exact local request before the browser sends it, plus accepted acknowledgement and artifact identities.
- original/browser-result.json joins source correction, native file export, capture, comparison, acceptance and ten original local actions.
- portfolio-migration-handover.html presents readable counts, accepted differences, identities and native transaction tables.
- portfolio-migration-handover.json preserves the full original deployment and comparison.
- The original portable ZIP retains source files, native exports, source and target editions, request/reply objects and acceptance.
- restore-intent.json and restore-receipt.json bind that same ZIP to its one receiving destination.
- restored-browser/browser-result.json verifies the same accepted project and exact handover bytes on the newly opened original workspace.
- result.json contains the full completed operation and artifact hashes.

The coordinator copies the selected fixture into its own input directory, then moves only that private copy aside before cold receiving. The exact copied bytes remain retained. The original upstream fixture is unchanged. The restored application reads its source and exports from the portable workspace.

Private browser entry files are temporary and owner-readable. Browser storage and operation control files remain private intermediates. Deliver the named source/report/ZIP artifacts and final result through the original customer operation.

## Meaning of the native file result

The file-target journey establishes the actual MPXJ reader/writer round trip through the product. The saved comparison carries every observed conversion difference and the receiving operator's acceptance decision. For an actual Project Operations environment, use the normal configured native target, original licensed user, scheduling OperationSets and MsPlannerReader capture described in the operator guide. That customer's existing target operation remains its own retained native state.

## Following archive phase

The complete portfolio reporting and source-preserving receiving phase is in ../../archive/native/README.md. Pass this operation's actual retained editions, original workspace and operation ID. It uses the same original browser/action helpers and adds no target acquisition or native submission. Keep the original results and append its complete archive receiving result to this handover.
